files.Summary: What a raise's list of cues belongs to: an effect, an ability, an entity or an item, by its asset; a cue tag; or a game's own code. A network layer names it by the asset's ID, or the tag's, in place of the cues themselves.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CuesAbilityComponent
files.Summary: Cues: what an ability shows and sounds at its moments, on its caster: as an activation starts, as it pays its cost and starts its cooldown, while it's active, as it ends, and as one is refused. A stage's exact moment plays through a Play Cue task. An ability holds one at most.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CuesEffectComponent
files.Summary: Cues: what an effect shows and sounds at its moments, on the one it's on: as it lands, as an application it takes in lands, as each of its ticks executes, as an impact it deals lands, as it comes off, while it lasts, as an application of it is refused, and as its stacks change. An effect holds one at most.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CuesEntityComponent
files.Summary: Cues: what an entity shows and sounds at its moments: as it comes into the game, dies and comes back, and, While Tagged, for as long as it holds a tag, as stars over its head while it's Stunned. An entity holds one at most.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CuesItemComponent
files.Summary: Cues: what an item shows and sounds on its holder: as it's equipped, while it's equipped, and as it's used, as an ability it lends is. A load that puts an equipped item back begins its lasting cues and plays no burst. An item holds one at most.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.CustomScaler
files.Summary: A scaler made of two delegates, one run as a carrier initializes it and one that works out its value, as IScaler.Generate makes. It isn't an AbstractScaler, so a number field can't hold it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.DashTask
files.Summary: Moves its caster toward its ability's target, or away from it, over a moment, as Tumble's roll. Its distance and duration are read as it starts, at its ability's level; it moves along the ground by its caster's time, a critical section, holding its caster's own mover, where it has one, while it moves. A caster with no object in the scene doesn't move.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.DataValue<T>
files.Summary: The entries of one type under a data packet's key, as GetAll and TryGetAll give them: the first (Primary), the Last, one at random (Any), All of them or each once (AllDistinct), or by an EDataTarget, and it enumerates them. IsValid where it holds any.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.DataWrapper
files.Summary: One entry of an asset's or an entity's Local Data: a value under a key. Its value is a class, a kind of its own: a number that can scale, a whole number, a string, a bool, a tag, an attribute, an effect, an ability, an entity, an object, a MonoBehaviour or a ScriptableObject; or a kind of your own, as a point or a colour, a [Serializable] class made from or , which is offered beside them. Each entry saves its own value alone.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.DeathAction
files.Summary: The deferred action that kills its entity as its turn comes, at Critical priority: the entity is marked dead, which its callbacks, its components, its effects and its killer hear, and it ends, or stays dead, at its frame's end, as its Death says. It's dropped where the entity is dead already; a death watcher and the Health role's watch queue it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.DeathWatcherAnalysisWorker
files.Summary: An analysis worker that kills its entity as an attribute reaches its threshold, as Health reaching 0: a Threshold whose firing queues the entity's death, after its effects and its event where it has them. An entity that holds one dies by it alone, not by its project's Health role reaching 0.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.DeferredContextSystem
files.Summary: The base of the subsystems of an entity that queue work for its end of frame, its attribute, ability and item systems and its analysis worker cache: it holds the entity's action queue and frame summary, which the GAS hands it through SetDeferredContext as it initializes.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.DelayTask
files.Summary: Waits: holds its stage for its delay, in its caster's time, read as it starts at its ability's level.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.DelegateSequenceInjection
files.Summary: An injection that does what a function of your own says: applyFunc is handed the run's runtime and returns whether it applied, as one that adds to a count on a key press or jumps to a stage by name. With no function it applies nothing.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.DelegateSequenceTask
files.Summary: Wraps a delegate as a sequence task.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.DelegateSyncTask
files.Summary: Wraps a delegate as a sync-first sequence task implementing the unified ISequenceTask. Step is the primary execution path; Execute bridges by looping Step with per-frame yields.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.DeriveScalerName
files.Summary: When placed on a Scaler field inside a ScalableFloat, the scaler drawer will look up the parent property's ScalerOperationKeyword attribute and use "{Keyword} Scaler" as the display name.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.DisjointAbilityTask
files.Summary: A stage task that makes its caster disjoint, as in Dota: each homing shot aimed at it whose data marks it disjointable loses it, flies on to where the caster stood and lands on nothing. A skill shot, which aims at no one, isn't touched.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.DisjointProxyTaskBehaviour
files.Summary: A disjoint, as in Dota: the shots already aimed at an entity lose it, fly on to where it stood, and land on nothing. A shot is found through the intent it registers with its target, which only a homing shot does (), and only one whose data marks it is disjointed. A skill shot, one that hits whatever it crosses, registers no intent, and lands as usual.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.DisjointTarget
files.Summary: The placeholder a disjointed shot is aimed at instead of its entity. It stays where the entity stood, has no tags, and takes no effects, so the shot lands on nothing.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.DurationChange
files.Summary: Changes how long it lasts: its time multiplied, then more added. Its ticks spread over the time it has.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAbilityActivationPolicy
files.Summary: What an activation does while another ability holds its claim, the When Busy the inspectors show. Activate Anyway (AlwaysActivate) starts at once; Refuse (ActivateIfIdle) is refused, as Busy, while another ability asked under Refuse holds its claim; Queue (QueueActivationIfBusy) waits in the input buffer, for up to its Buffer Window, while a Queue ability holds its claim or a running stage blocks it. Whatever the choice, an ability with critical tasks can't start while another with critical tasks holds its claim. An entity's When Busy is one, and so is each activation request's Policy.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAbilityActivationPolicyExtended
files.Summary: An ability's When Busy as its Definition holds it: Entity's Policy (UseLocalPolicy), the default, takes its entity's When Busy, and the others are the EAbilityActivationPolicy choices, Activate Anyway, Refuse and Queue. TryActivateAbility and CreateActivationRequest can name one in place of the ability's.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAbilityEffectRole
files.Summary: How an effect participates in an ability.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAbilityEnd
files.Summary: How an ability's activation ended.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAbilityLinkMode
files.Summary: Defines how an ability is linked to its level provider.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAbilityPart
files.Summary: What an Asset Part number reads of an ability.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAbilityStageConditionSubject
files.Summary: Where a stage's condition looks for its tag.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAbilityTriggerSource
files.Summary: What sets an ability off on its own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EActionStatus
files.Summary: How a composite behaviour's run on one user came out, as its Status reads it: Success; Pending, not yet done; Failure, refused by its checks, as a shot not marked disjointable; Error, as with a caller that isn't an entity; NoData, nothing recorded for the user; or NoOp, nothing done, as for a shot whose data says nothing of being disjointable.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EActivationRefusal
files.Summary: Why an activation was refused, or None where it wasn't: it activated, waits in the input buffer, or starts next frame. A refused activation said only false.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EActivationStatus
files.Summary: What came of a request to activate an ability.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAddBehaviour
files.Summary: How an Add impacter combines with the others on its attribute.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAffiliationFilter
files.Summary: Whom a search or a check takes, by how each stands to its caster, or to an aura's holder: an enemy shares none of its sides, an ally shares one, and the caster itself is an ally of itself and no one's enemy. The one choice an Area Effect, an effect's area, a spread, an aura, the auto-target tasks and an Affiliation check make. A caster with no sides takes every other one as its ally and its enemy alike.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAffiliationPolicy
files.Summary: Which targets an effect may land on, by their affiliation tags against its origin's: Always Allow, the default, takes any; Affiliated, those that share the origin's sides; Unaffiliated, those that don't; Use Affiliation List, those that carry the effect's own Affiliations. The impact's Comparison says whether one tag matching does or every tag must, and a target it doesn't take refuses the effect.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAnyAllPolicy
files.Summary: How a list of tags is matched against another: Any passes where one of its tags is in the other, All only where every one is. An effect's Affiliation Comparison is one, and so is the Context Matching Policy of a focused attribute worker and of a context impact worker.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EApplyTickRemove
files.Summary: The moment in an effect's life another effect lands at: as it's applied (On Apply), on each of its execute ticks (On Tick), or as it's removed (On Remove). A contained effect and an effect a modifier adds each name one; an Instant effect has no ticks and no removal, so only its On Apply ones land.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAreaCentre
files.Summary: Where an area search is measured from.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAssetPartAmong
files.Summary: How an Asset Part number reads one value from several that match.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAssetPartOf
files.Summary: What an Asset Part number looks for on an entity.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAttributeChangeWhat
files.Summary: What an Attribute Change worker answers about its attribute.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAttributeElementCollisionPolicy
files.Summary: An attribute set element's Collision: the group it joins where its attribute appears in more than one element across a set and its sub-sets. One group decides the attribute's root, the first there is of Use Set Collision Setting, Use This, Combine and Use Existing, and the other groups' elements are passed over: Combine adds its elements' values up, and each other group picks one, or averages them, by the Resolution Policy of the set the entity names.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAttributeOverflowPolicy
files.Summary: The bounds an attribute set element holds its attribute's values in, with its Floor and Ceiling, each a Current and a Base: Zero To Base holds Current between 0 and Base; Floor To Base, Current between the Floor's Current and Base, and Base at or above the Floor's Base; Zero To Ceil, each between 0 and the Ceiling's; Floor To Ceil, each between its Floor and its Ceiling; Unlimited, none. They hold only while the element's Auto Clamp is on.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAttributeRead
files.Summary: How × Attribute reads its attribute.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAttributeRole
files.Summary: What an attribute is, which sets how bonuses to it add up and how a number reads it by default, as how several effects' Damage Amplification adds up and how an attack's scaler reads it. An effect's impact can add up its own way, and a number can read it its own way.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAttributeRoundingPolicy
files.Summary: How an attribute set element rounds its attribute's Current and Base, after its bounds, each time the value changes: None; To Floor, down; To Ceil, up; Round, to the nearest; Snap To, to the nearest multiple of its Snap Interval. Rounding can make a change bigger or smaller than its effect asked for.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAttributeSetLinkMode
files.Summary: Defines how an AttributeSet's level range is sourced.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAttributeTarget
files.Summary: Which of an attribute's two values a change goes to: its Current, its Base, or both. An effect's impact names one with its operation, as Add to Current or Multiply Base, and a transfer's Slot and a threshold effect worker's Target choose by it too.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAttributeTargetBinary
files.Summary: The part of an attribute's value something reads: its Current, its Base, what's missing of it (base − current), or its share (current ÷ base), as AttributeParts.Read reads it. A Threshold, a wait, the Attribute condition and an attribute-backed number read through it; some fields, as a tracked impact's part or a retention group's, read Base under Base and Current otherwise.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAttributeTargetExpanded
files.Summary: Which of an attribute's values a change must touch for a worker to take it: Current, Base, Current And Base, or Current Or Base. A focused attribute worker's Target Modification and a context impact worker's Impact Target choose by it; with their exclusive switch on, a change to Current or to Base must touch that one alone.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAttributeTargetLimited
files.Summary: A narrower EAttributeTarget, of the two choices that change Base: Current and Base together, or Base alone. ForgeHelper.Translate gives the EAttributeTarget it names.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EAutoTargetMode
files.Summary: How an auto-targeting task, Auto Target or Auto Target By Affinity, orders the entities it finds before it takes its Max Targets, the first being its primary target: Nearest or Farthest first, measured from where its range is, or in a Random order; All leaves them as found. Max Targets still holds under All, and 0 takes every one.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ECalculationOperation
files.Summary: How a change applies its magnitude to an attribute's value: Add adds it, Multiply multiplies by it, FlatBonus adds it after the multipliers, so they don't scale it, and Override sets the value to it. An attribute's lasting modifiers apply in that order, and of several overrides of one value the lowest order wins. An effect's impact chooses one as its Operation, and some workers do.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ECaptureAttributeWhen
files.Summary: When a × Attribute scaler reads its attribute: OnCreation captures it once, as the effect's spec is made, and reads that snapshot after; OnApplication reads the live value each time the scaler is read.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EChangeStepKind
files.Summary: What a step of a change to an attribute was.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ECombatLogKind
files.Summary: What a combat log entry is.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ECombatLogRecords
files.Summary: What an entity's combat log writes, as the project subscribes to it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EComparisonOperator
files.Summary: How one number compares with another: less than, less or equal, equal, not equal, greater or equal, or greater than. A tag query compares the tag's count with its number by it, and conditions, validation rules, waits, auto-targeting and the threshold effect worker compare their numbers by it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ECrowdControlStops
files.Summary: What a crowd control rule stops.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ECueAt
files.Summary: Whom a cue places what it plays on.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ECueAttach
files.Summary: Whether what a cue places follows what it's placed at.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ECueEvent
files.Summary: How a cue plays: a burst, or a lasting cue's beginning or its end.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ECueFacing
files.Summary: Which way what a cue places faces.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ECueMoment
files.Summary: What raised a cue: one of an effect's moments, an ability's, an entity's or an item's, or a game's own code.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ECueSource
files.Summary: What a raise's list of cues belongs to.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ECurveTangentMode
files.Summary: Runtime-safe mirror of the editor tangent modes used by scaler curves.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EDataTarget
files.Summary: Which entry under a data packet's key a read takes where the key holds several: Primary, the first; Any, one at random; or Last, the last.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EDeathPolicy
files.Summary: What an entity's death does.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EEffectCategory
files.Summary: The kinds of effect a death can keep whatever their tiers.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EEffectDurationPolicy
files.Summary: How long an effect lives: Instant, the default, makes its change once and is done; Durational stays on the target's shelf for its Duration; Infinite stays until something removes it. It gives the effect's first impact its delivery: on applying for an Instant effect, and for a lasting one while it lasts, or on each tick where it ticks.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EEffectInteractionPolicy
files.Summary: What a lasting effect on the target does with its time as it takes in an application under Do Nothing, Replace Existing or Stack Existing: Do Nothing, the default, leaves it; Refresh Duration restarts it; Extend Duration adds the new application's duration to it, or, where stacks keep their own durations, adds a stack. Refresh and Extend run Tick On Application again.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EEffectJournalKind
files.Summary: What an effect journal's entry tells.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EEffectLinkMode
files.Summary: Defines how an effect is linked to its level provider.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EEffectPart
files.Summary: What an Asset Part number reads of an effect.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EEffectReApplicationPolicy
files.Summary: What a Durational or Infinite effect does as it's applied to a target that has it already, matched by its asset tag whoever applied it: Add Another, the default, adds a container of its own; Do Nothing takes nothing new in; Replace Existing gives the old container the new application's values and modifiers, keeping its stacks and past commits; Stack Existing adds stacks to it. All but Add Another then do with its time as the effect's EEffectInteractionPolicy says.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EEffectRecipient
files.Summary: Whom an effect another lands lands on: a contained effect, an overflow's, or one a modifier adds.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EEffectRefusal
files.Summary: Why an effect didn't land on an entity, as the entity's callbacks tell it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EEffectStackPolicy
files.Summary: How the stacks of an effect whose Re-application is Stack Existing keep time: Stacks Share One Duration, the default, runs one timer for all, which a stack added doesn't reset, each tick executing once for each stack; Stacks Have Independent Durations gives each stack its own timer and ticks, so they drop off one at a time; Duration Taken From One Stack runs one stack's timer at a time, a stack lost and the timer restarted each time it runs out.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EEffectTargetScope
files.Summary: Who an effect application lands on, as statically determinable.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EEffectWorkerHook
files.Summary: The moment of its effect an effect worker heard.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EEventRecipient
files.Summary: Whom a Send Event task sends to: its caster, or each of its activation's targets.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EFacingCheck
files.Summary: Which way a Facing check looks.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EFloatingValue
files.Summary: Where a floating text's number comes from.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EFromSelfSource
files.Summary: Where a relative attribute worker reads its relative attribute: From Self, on the entity whose attribute changes; From Source, on the source of the change.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EGroupOperation
files.Summary: How a Group's member joins the others: an impact's four operations, in their order, so a member saved before keeps its meaning, and Divide.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EGroupOverflowPolicy
files.Summary: What happens when a new member tries to join a full group.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EImpactDelivery
files.Summary:
How an impact entry rides its carrier's lifecycle. Delivery IMPLIES the contribution kind — there is deliberately no independent "retained?" switch to get wrong:

  • → Modifier (transient, derived). Registered while the carrier is present, re-evaluated on every recompute, reversed automatically and exactly when the carrier is removed. Only valid on durational/infinite carriers.
  • → Commit (permanent). One commit at application time. Never reversed. This is what an Instant effect is.
  • → Commit (permanent) once per execute tick. Never reversed. Requires a carrier with periodic ticks enabled.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EItemLinkMode
files.Summary: Defines how an item is linked to its level provider.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EItemPart
files.Summary: What an Asset Part number reads of an item.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EJournalActionState
files.Summary: Where an action a worker queued stands.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ELevelConfig
files.Summary: The level range a scaler's values spread over, where they spread: the level provider's (LockToLevelProvider, Provider's Levels), the scaler's own Max Level (Unlocked, Own Max Level), or the provider's up to that Max Level (Clamped, Clamped to Provider), so the values reach their last at the lower of the two.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ELocalDataFrom
files.Summary: Whose Local Data a Local Data number reads.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EMagnitudeOperation
files.Summary: How a field joins its number with its scaler, its Combine: Multiply With Scaler, the scaler times the number; Add Scaler, the scaler plus the number; Use Magnitude, the number alone; Use Scaler, the scaler alone. A number field, an attribute set element's sides, an effect's clock and Scaled Stack Amount each combine by it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EMathApplicationPolicy
files.Summary: How a value is used as a factor: AsIs as it is, OnePlus as 1 + x, and OneMinus as 1 − x, so a 30% bonus multiplies by 1.3 and a 30% reduction by 0.7. An Attenuate scaler behaviour's Policy turns its value so, and a Math attribute worker's Operation Policy the attribute it changes by.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EModifierDirection
files.Summary: Which effects a modifier changes: those its holder applies, those landing on it, or both.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EMultiplyBehaviour
files.Summary: How a Multiply impact combines with the other multiplies on the same value of its attribute: Multiplicative, the default, compounds them, ×1.5 and ×1.5 making ×2.25; Additive Bonus adds each one's bonus, its value less 1, and multiplies once, +50% and +50% making ×2.0. It's apart from stacking, which decides how one effect applied again stacks against itself.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EOnHitTo
files.Summary: Whom an On Hit's effects land on.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EProcessAttributeStart
files.Summary: Where a process's own attribute starts.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EProcessControlState
files.Summary: What ProcessControl does as a whole: Ready takes new processes and runs them; Waiting takes them and holds every process where it is; Closed takes no more and runs those it has; ClosedWaiting takes no more and holds those it has; Terminated ends every process, a running one as its run ends, and TerminatedImmediately ends them all at once, and neither takes more. SetControlState sets it, and leaving a waiting state sends back what it held; the inspector's Start State is the one it starts in.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EProcessLifecycle
files.Summary: How a process starts and what follows its run: SelfTerminating starts running and ends as its run is done, as a projectile; RunThenWait starts running and waits when its run is done, to run again, as an ability; RequiresControl starts waiting and runs only when told, as an ability on a key; and Synchronous starts running with no run to await, stepped at its timing for as long as it lasts, as a health bar.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EProcessRegistrationRefusal
files.Summary: Why ProcessControl refused a registration, or None when it took the process.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EProcessState
files.Summary: Where a registered process is in its life: Created, as it's registered and set up, before its first move; Running; Waiting, paused or waiting to run again; and Terminated, ended and cleaned up. A relay's State reads it, and the process's lifecycle and ProcessControl's state decide each move.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EProcessStatus
files.Summary: Whether a process is stepped or its run awaited, as its wrapper's Status says: Synchronous for a process of the Synchronous lifecycle, Asynchronous for any other, and Unknown where the wrapper doesn't say.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EProcessStepPriorityMethod
files.Summary: Where a process steps among the others of its timing: First, at priority 0; Last, after every other; or Manual, at its own step priority. Lower priorities step first, and ProcessControl registers a scene's own processes by it too, parents before their children.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EProcessStepTiming
files.Summary: Which of Unity's loops a process is stepped in while it runs, each step calling its WhenUpdate, WhenLateUpdate or WhenFixedUpdate: one of Update, LateUpdate and FixedUpdate, two of them, all three, or None, never stepped. A GAS hub steps in Update and LateUpdate: Update ticks its effects, and LateUpdate runs its end of frame. Under ProcessControl's Fixed Tick Rate, each tick steps the Update and LateUpdate processes.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EPurgeRelation
files.Summary: Whom a purge takes the effects of, by who applied each, against the one purged.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ERequireAvoidPolicy
files.Summary: Which way a tag worker's requirement holds: Require, while the tag's weight on the entity is at least the required weight; Avoid, while it's below it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ERetentionGroupRead
files.Summary: Which of an attribute's retention groups a read takes.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ERoundingOperation
files.Summary: How a whole-number field, a ScalableInt, makes a value read through its scaler whole: Floor rounds it down, Ceil up, and Round to the nearest, a half away from zero. Scaled Stack Amount rounds its stacks by it too.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ESavedOrigin
files.Summary: The kinds of origin a save tells apart.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EScalerInterpolation
files.Summary: How a scaler whose values spread over levels reads a level between two of its points: Constant steps from one to the next (Steps), Linear goes in a straight line (Straight Line), and Smooth along a smooth curve (Smooth Curve).

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EScalerParts
files.Summary: The parts of every scaler a kind reads, which its inspector draws ().

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EScalerRelativeOperation
files.Summary: How a cached attribute-backed scaler joins the attribute it captures with its own value at the level: Add adds them, Multiply multiplies them, and UseAttributeValue and UseScalerValue take one alone.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ESideSource
files.Summary: Whose sides a side-changing effect gives its target.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ESignPolicy
files.Summary: The sign of a change or a value: Positive, Negative, ZeroBiased, 0 from values that cancel out, or ZeroNeutral, 0 from nothing at all. ForgeHelper.SignPolicy reads it from magnitudes and an attribute change's SignPolicy gives it; a context impact worker takes impacts of one sign (Impact Sign) and gives its own change one (Work Sign Policy).

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ESignPolicyExtended
files.Summary: A sign policy with Any, which every sign matches: a focused attribute worker's Sign Policy, the sign of the changes it watches, is one.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ESourceTarget
files.Summary: Which side's attribute is read: the Source, whose effect or impact it is, or the Target. A × Attribute scaler's Capture From chooses one, as does a RelativeOperationContextImpactWorker's With Respect To.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ESpreadMoment
files.Summary: The moments a Spread component spreads at.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EStackBoundsOnMaxPolicy
files.Summary: What Stack Bounds does as an application finds the effect at its Max: Do Nothing, the default, keeps to the one effect, held at its Max; Append New Container stacks it into a container of the effect under its Max, or else a new one, which stacks again.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EStackingCurve
files.Summary: How a stacking curve turns a count into its number, with its a.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EStopImpacts
files.Summary: What a Block or Evade stage can stop.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ESyncStagePolicy
files.Summary: Completion policy for synchronous stages.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ETagChangeKind
files.Summary: What a tag listener hears.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ETagMatchMode
files.Summary: Mode for matching tags in queries.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ETagWait
files.Summary: What a Wait For Tag task waits for: its tag gained, or lost.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EThresholdComparison
files.Summary: How a Threshold analysis worker compares what it reads with its threshold while its Crossing is While It Holds: less than, less than or equal, greater than, greater than or equal, or equal, within 0.001.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EThresholdCrossing
files.Summary: As a threshold fires.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EThresholdSource
files.Summary: Whom a threshold's effects come from.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ETrackedImpactOf
files.Summary: Whose impacts a Tracked Impact number reads.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ETrackedImpactPart
files.Summary: What a Tracked Impact number reads of what effects have dealt.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ETriggerImpactSign
files.Summary: Which way an impact goes, for a trigger that takes impact events.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ETriggerTarget
files.Summary: What an ability a trigger sets off targets.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.ETurnTooLong
files.Summary: What a turn to face a target does when reaching its Start Angle takes longer than its Max Wait.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EUsageCheck
files.Summary: The checks of an ability's use a component may waive, : its cost, as the Cost check asks, and its cooldown, as the Cooldown check asks.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EValidationSide
files.Summary: Which of an ability's checks a rule belongs among: its Caster Checks, its Target Checks, or either.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EValueCollisionPolicy
files.Summary: Which value stands where several claim one result: the highest (UseMaximum), the lowest, their average, the first or the last, or none of them (Ignore). A Group's policy picks among its overriding members, Ignore setting them aside so the rest join as they would; an attribute set's Resolution Policy picks among the elements that give one attribute, Ignore keeping the first.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EWhileTargeting
files.Summary: What an ability still choosing its target does as another of its entity's abilities activates, past that one's own checks, on a request that cancels targeting (CancelsTargeting), as a player's press does: the While Targeting the inspectors show. Entity's Rule (EntitysRule) does as its entity's Targeting Yields says; Yields gives way, its targeting cancelled, nothing of it paid, and its claim let go at once, so the other starts; Holds keeps its claim until its target is chosen or it's cancelled, and the other does as its When Busy says.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EWorkerExecution
files.Summary: Defines how a worker executes during the modification pipeline.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EWorkerNumberFrom
files.Summary: Whose workers a Worker number asks.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EWorkerSide
files.Summary: Whose side a worker ran on: the entity its effect is on, or the one that dealt the hit, as an effect's workers hear its hits on their dealer's side and impact workers run for their dealer.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.EachChargeRecharge
files.Summary: Each spent charge comes back on a cooldown of its own, run alongside the others: the default.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbilityBehaviourDrawer
files.Summary: An ability's behaviour drawn whole, as an asset or a component of the user's own holds one: Unity's foldout of the fields the ability inspector shows of it, its targeting, its asset loaders, what cancels it and what it blocks, and its stages. The lists are Unity's, where a new loader starts empty and each stage keeps its fold as one is removed or dragged; Implicit Tag shows under Use Implicit Targeting while it's on. It drew colored sections that folded, lists of its own, and badges.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbilityComponentDrawer
files.Summary: An ability's component: its kind, never None and named without "AbilityComponent", as "Cast Range" for a CastRangeAbilityComponent, then its fields, folding to a line of their values. A kind an ability may hold only once isn't offered while its list holds one.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbilityDrawer
files.Summary: A reference to an ability: Unity's object field, with Open or New beside it. It was a button that opened a dropdown list of its own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbilityEditor
files.Summary: The Ability inspector: Identity, Leveling, Tags, the ability's Activation and Stages, Requirements, Workers and Local Data, then Used By. A collapsed section shows one line, and the inspector takes its look from the style sheet.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbilityStageConditionDrawer
files.Summary: A stage's condition: its tag, a tag field in the label column, and, once it names one, where the stage looks for it and whether it runs while the tag is missing instead, each indented under it. With no tag, the stage always runs, and Unity's foldout showed all three.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbilityTagRequirementsDrawer
files.Summary: An ability's tag requirements, as the same table: the caster's, the caster's while the ability runs, and the target's, each with what it requires and what it must not have.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbilityTaskBehaviourStageDrawer
files.Summary:
An ability's stage: a foldout row named by its place, as "Stage 1", with Critical on its right while a task commits the ability to it; folded, one line of what it holds, as "2 tasks · All · Applies usage effects"; open, its completion policy, its usage effects, its condition, what cancels it and what it blocks, then its tasks in Unity's reorderable list, where a new task starts empty. The stages' own list removes a stage.

It drew a colored badge for the stage's number, its policy, its usage effects, its task count and a critical task, ▶ and ▼ as text, a delete button, and a list of its own with ▲, ▼ and × buttons, from 163 styles set in C#; and it grew that list as an array, which gave a new task the last one's object, so the two were one.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbilityTaskDrawer
files.Summary: An ability task: its kind, as "Delay" for a DelayTask, then the kind's own fields. The base drawer names a kind without "AbilityTask" or "Task", and builds the fields again as the kind changes, which this drawer did itself.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbilityValidationRuleDrawer
files.Summary: An ability's validation rule: its kind, as its [ForgeMenu] names it or named without "ValidationRule" or "Validation", then the kind's own fields. A rule is always of some kind, so the picker offers no None. Each list is offered the kinds of its side, the Caster Checks a caster's and the Target Checks a target's, with those of either; a check a component stands behind, as Check Range, is offered to neither, as it comes with its component.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbstractComponentDrawer<T>
files.Summary: A component: its kind, always of some kind, then its fields. A kind that allows one is offered while the list it's in holds none of it, the element that holds it still naming it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbstractForgeObjectDrawer<T>
files.Summary: A reference to a PlayForge asset, or to a Value Pipeline, Crowd Control Rules or Effect Modifier: Unity's object field, with its type's icon, and beside it a plain button, Open while it names an asset, which shows the asset in a window of its own, or New while it's empty, which asks for a new one's name in The Forge's New dialog, makes it where The Forge makes its type and uses it. A drawer adds its own actions to the field's right-click menu. It was a button that opened a dropdown list of its own, with hover colors and Clear and Open icon buttons set in C#.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbstractGenericDrawer<T>
files.Summary: A kind field that folds, as an attribute set element does: a row with the arrow and the kind field, then the kind's fields; folded, one line of their values in secondary text, as "Strength 2 · Duration 0.5". Whether it's folded is kept with the object the field holds, so it follows the object through its list. It drew colored badges for a folded field's values, and its arrow and its look from styles set in C#.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbstractMonoProcessEditor
files.Summary:
A Mono Process's inspector: a Process section of Unity's fields, its lifecycle, its timing, how it's ordered as it steps, how it's made, and whether it follows its siblings, each choice saying what it does in its field's tooltip; then the component's own fields. Priority Method shows while the process steps, and Priority under it while the method is Manual. It drew a tinted box, a gray hint in 10 px under each field, set 50 ms after it drew, and a gray rule.

Every field is a PropertyField bound to its property, so a multiple selection edits each process, and a prefab instance's edits show as overrides. Without [CanEditMultipleObjects] the Inspector never offered one.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbstractTypeRefDrawer<T>
files.Summary:
A [SerializeReference] field of an abstract type: Unity's field, its label in the label column, the kind it holds named in its box, which opens Unity's searchable dropdown of the kinds it can hold; then the kind's own fields, each Unity's, indented under it. A pick makes a new object of the kind for each selected asset, by the kind's constructor so its initializers run, as one Undo step; drawing writes nothing.

Every element of a list shares one drawer, so each field keeps its state in its own elements. The drawer kept the last element's fields and kind in fields of its own, so an edit to one element could fill another with its fields. It drew a button that opened a list in tinted boxes, and the kind's fields in a box with an orange left border.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AbstractWorkerDrawer<T>
files.Summary: A worker: its kind, always of some kind, then its fields, folding to a line of their values.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AlignedFoldoutDrawer
files.Summary: Each class PlayForge serializes in a field with no drawer of its own, drawn as a foldout of its fields, its arrow in line with the rows around it, as a list's is: an attribute read's retention groups, as an × Attribute scaler's Groups, a turn to face's settings, an asset's definition and tags, a list's entries. Unity hangs an inspector foldout's arrow 12 px into the margin, to the left of a list's arrow and, in a scaler's block, out to the block's edge; this one keeps the lists' column, as pf-foldout--aligned sets in PlayForge.uss. A class opts in with a of its type here. A field marked shows only while the field it names says so, as a read's Groups shows only for the reads that name groups. An inspector drawn with IMGUI gets the same foldout.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AnalysisWorkerDrawer
files.Summary: An analysis worker, as a worker group's Analysis list holds one: its kind, picked from the analysis workers or None, then its fields, folding to a line of their values.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AssetSetterDrawer
files.Summary: An asset loader, as an ability's Asset Loaders list holds one: its kind, picked from the Set tasks, as "Set Effects" for a SetEffectsTask, then the kind's own fields.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeConstraintsDrawer
files.Summary: An attribute's constraints: Auto Clamp, Scale With Base and Rounding, Unity's fields in the label column, with Snap Interval indented under Rounding while it snaps. They sat in a tinted, rounded box with a yellow left border, under a 10 px bold heading with colored letter badges, from styles set in C#.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeCostDrawer
files.Summary: An ability's attribute cost: the attribute it spends, or, where it names none, the role whose attribute it spends, and how much.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeDrawer
files.Summary: A reference to an attribute: Unity's object field, with Open or New beside it. It was a button that opened a dropdown list of its own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeEditor
files.Summary: The Attribute asset's inspector, which edits several attributes at once: its header, then Identity (Name, Abbreviation, Description, Role and, for a Barrier, what it absorbs for and how it decays, Gains Scaled By, the roles it plays in its project, and Textures), Local Data, and Used By, the assets that refer to it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeImpactEntryDrawer
files.Summary: One of an effect's additional impacts: a foldout row with its attribute and a Remove button, and while it's folded one line such as "Mana −10 · Continuous"; open, its operation, magnitude and delivery, then its order, retention group and impact types. Its Delivery offers what the effect's duration can make, and a help box says when the one it names can't happen. An impact entry had no drawer, so an effect couldn't be given a second impact.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeOverflowDataDrawer
files.Summary: An attribute's bounds: the policy, then the floor and the ceiling it reads, each indented under it, as a field that depends on another is. A bound's right-click menu sets it to no limit. It drew the floor and ceiling with 10 px labels and buttons in an accent color, from styles set in C#, and showed them 50 ms after it drew.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeRoleDrawer
files.Summary: A project's role on one row: its tag, then the attribute that plays it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeSetDrawer
files.Summary: A reference to an attribute set: Unity's object field, with Open or New beside it. It was a button that opened a dropdown list of its own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeSetEditor
files.Summary: The Attribute Set inspector: Identity, Leveling, the set's Attributes, Sub-Sets and Collision Settings, then All Attributes, the table of what the set gives an entity, then Workers, Local Data and Used By. A collapsed section shows one line, and the inspector takes its look from the style sheet.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeSetElementDrawer
files.Summary:
An attribute set element: a foldout row with the attribute, and while it's folded one line of what it starts at; open, what it starts at at each level, then Base and Current, each a magnitude field as an effect's are, then its bounds, its constraints, its retention group and its collision.

What it starts at is worked out by the runtime (): a stand-in entity at each level of the set it's previewed in, with the set's sub-sets. A note says when another element's value is the one used, and a message when a scaler reads an attribute the set doesn't give. The element showed its magnitudes as a formula, as "10 + Level", and Current and Base one at a time on a switch.

It writes nothing while it draws, and only a typed magnitude is kept within the bounds, as part of the same edit.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeStartValues.Result
files.Summary: What a set's attributes start at, over its levels.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeStartValues.Start
files.Summary: One attribute's start: its value at each level, and the elements that give it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeStartValues
files.Summary: What each attribute an entity built from an attribute set starts at, at each of the set's levels, worked out as the runtime works it out: a stand-in entity at the level, whose attribute system is set up from the set as the GAS sets one up, with the set's sub-sets and collisions, and each element's scalers, bounds and rounding. Nothing else acts on the stand-in, no worker, effect or item, so a value is the one the set gives before anything changes it. A set that another holds starts as part of it, so its values can be worked out in each set that holds it, and the attribute set inspector previews a set in one of them ().

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeTransferDrawer
files.Summary: An effect's transfer: when it moves, who gives and of what, who gets and in what, which of the values, and how much, each a field of its own as an attribute cost's are.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeValueDrawer
files.Summary: An attribute value: its label in the label column, then its Current and Base side by side. It drew "Cur" and "Base" in 9 px text with a slash between them, from styles set in C#.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AttributeWorkerDrawer
files.Summary: An attribute worker, as a worker group's Attribute list holds one: its kind, picked from the attribute workers and never None, then its fields, folding to a line of their values.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AuraEntryDrawer
files.Summary: An aura's fields, drawn where it's held, as an Aura component's own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.AvoidRequireTagGroupDrawer
files.Summary: A requirement group of its own, as a targeting task's or a template's: the same table, of one row named by the field, with what it requires and what it must not have; a cell opens its list, with the group's name and template under it. It drew a tinted box with green and red stripes, colored count badges, a Name and an Import of its own, and rebuilt itself as it opened.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.BasePlayForgeEditor
files.Summary: Base class for all PlayForge asset inspectors: a header with the asset's name and type, and the content below it. The content scrolls in the Inspector's own scroll view, and the header stays at its top.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.BuildVerification
files.Summary: Headless player-build verification (asset-store readiness / CI): Unity -batchmode -nographics -projectPath <proj> -executeMethod FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.BuildVerification.BuildWindowsPlayer Exit codes: 0 = build succeeded, 1 = build failed, 3 = exception. Proves the runtime assembly compiles and links in a real player (no editor-only leaks).

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.CachedMagnitudeModifierGroupMemberDrawer
files.Summary: A Scaler Group's member, cached or not, as Unity's fields: how its result combines with the members' before it, then its scaler, whose own drawer shows its kind and its settings. It drew a stripe and a symbol in the operation's color, the scaler's kind beside them, and, for a cached member, a "CACHED" badge.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ChanceRollDrawer
files.Summary: How a chance rolls, as Unity's foldout of its fields: Pseudo-Random, Own Luck, and Luck while Own Luck is on, where it's read; without it the project's Luck role is read, so Luck is hidden.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ChargeRechargeDrawer
files.Summary: An ability's Recharge: its kind, named without "Recharge", as Each Charge or All At Once, or one of your own, then the kind's own fields. A recharge is always of some kind, so the picker offers no None.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ClockChoiceDrawer
files.Summary: A clock picked in an inspector, as an ability's Run Sequence task's Clock: its kind, Caster's, Game's, Unscaled or Scaled, or one of your own, then the kind's own fields, as Scaled's Scale and the clock it scales. None leaves the run the clock it would have had.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ConditionDrawer
files.Summary: A condition field, as a Conditional scaler's When, drawn as a scaler field is: its name and its kind, picked from the conditions there are, a project's own among them, its one line, as "Target's Health < 0.3 × Target's Health (base)", then the condition's own fields on a block under it, each as Unity draws its type, so its numbers are number fields. It writes nothing while it draws.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ContainedEffectPacketDrawer
files.Summary: A contained effect, on one row: when it's applied, then the effect. It drew a tinted, rounded box with a stripe in its policy's color, set 50 ms after it drew.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ContextImpactWorkerDrawer
files.Summary: A context impact worker, one made from AbstractContextImpactWorker: its kind, picked from those workers or None, then its fields, folding to a line of their values.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.CrowdControlRuleDrawer
files.Summary: A crowd control rule: its tag, what it stops, and, where it stops the abilities carrying one of its tags, those tags. A stun stops every ability, so its row names none.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.CrowdControlRulesDrawer
files.Summary: A Crowd Control Rules field as a reference to an asset, with New and Open beside it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.CrowdControlRulesEditor
files.Summary: A Crowd Control Rules asset's inspector: the shared header, then its rules.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.CueHandlerDrawer
files.Summary: A cue handler, picked by its kind, as a worker is.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.CueLibraryEditor
files.Summary: A cue library's inspector: its routes, each a cue tag and the handlers it plays; then each cue tag the project's assets raise through it, by a Cue Tag cue, with the route that plays it, or that none does, and the assets that raise it, each a row that opens its asset in The Forge. It follows the project as it changes, and its routes as they're edited.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.DataWrapperDrawer
files.Summary: A Local Data row: its key, its value's kind and its value, each a column of its own, laid out by the style sheet. A value's kind is a class, Float to ScriptableObject or one of your own: a kind that holds one Value draws it in the row, and one of your own with more fields draws each under its name. Each row holds a value of its own, so a row added as a copy of the last edits its own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.EffectAreaDrawer
files.Summary: An effect's area's fields, drawn where it's held, as an Area component's own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.EffectChangeDrawer
files.Summary: A modifier's change: its kind, always of some kind, then its fields, as a worker is drawn.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.EffectComponentDrawer
files.Summary: An effect's component: its kind, never None and named without "EffectComponent", as "Aura" for an AuraEffectComponent, then its fields, folding to a line of their values. A kind an effect may hold only once isn't offered while its list holds one.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.EffectModifierDrawer
files.Summary: An Effect Modifier field as a reference to an asset, with New and Open beside it.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.EffectModifierEditor
files.Summary: An Effect Modifier's inspector: what it's for, its rule, the effects it picks and its changes, each of a kind with its fields, and a line that says them. Unity's own fields.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.EffectPurgeDrawer
files.Summary: An effect's Purges, a foldout of its fields, its arrow in line with the lists' around it in the Tags section. Unity hangs an inspector foldout's arrow 12 px into the margin, to the left of a list's arrow; this one keeps the lists' column, as pf-foldout--aligned sets in PlayForge.uss.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.EffectTagRequirementsDrawer
files.Summary: An effect's tag requirements on one side, the target's or the source's, as a table: Applying, While On and Removed By, each with what it requires and what it must not have. The drawer drew a tinted box with colored subsections, a type badge, a Name and import buttons of its own, and rebuilt itself as it opened.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.EffectTemplateRegistry
files.Summary: The effects a new Cost or Cooldown effect copies, by "Cost" or "Cooldown". Project Settings → PlayForge holds them, with the project; they lived in EditorPrefs, which every project on the machine shares.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.EffectWorkerDrawer
files.Summary: An effect worker, as an effect's Workers list holds one: its kind, picked from the effect workers or None, then its fields, folding to a line of their values.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.EntityComponentDrawer
files.Summary: An entity's component: its kind, never None and named without "EntityComponent", as "Respawn" for a RespawnEntityComponent, then its fields, folding to a line of their values. A kind an entity may hold only once isn't offered while its list holds one.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.EntityDrawer
files.Summary: A reference to an entity: Unity's object field, with Open or New beside it. It was a button that opened a dropdown list of its own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.EntityIdentityEditor
files.Summary: The Entity inspector: Identity, Leveling, Tags, the entity's Attributes, Abilities and Items, Workers and Local Data, then Used By. A collapsed section shows one line, and the inspector takes its look from the style sheet.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.FocusedAttributeWorkerDrawer
files.Summary: A focused attribute worker, one made from AbstractFocusedAttributeWorker: its kind, picked from those workers and never None, then its fields, folding to a line of their values.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeAssetLines
files.Summary: One line for each asset, which its inspector's header and The Forge's list show: an ability's numbers by level, then its costs and cooldown, as "-450/-600/-750 Health; 280/420/680 Mana; 70/60/50 s"; an item's what it changes while equipped and the ability it grants, as "+20 Armor; Blink"; an entity's first attributes as it starts and its abilities, as "Health 500, Mana 300, Armor 5; Fireball, Blink"; an effect's first impact by level, as its Levels section reads it. Numbers that read what an editor can't give, as the target, are marked with a *.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeComponentRule<TComponent>
files.Summary: A check of one kind of component, wherever an asset holds it: an ability's, an effect's, an item's or an entity's. The validator finds it as it finds every rule, and it hears each component of its kind the asset holds, with the component's place in its list, which a problem names as its property path; an ability's inspector says its problems under the Components list. Derive from it, with a public constructor that takes nothing, for a component of your own, as PlayForge's components' rules do.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeDrawerStyles.Colors
files.Summary: The colors PlayForge's editors draw with: accents and section tints, backgrounds, text and borders, status colors, and a color for each kind of PlayForge asset, which GetAssetColor gives for a type, gray for any it doesn't name.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeDrawerStyles.HeaderConfig
files.Summary: Configuration for main header creation.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeDrawerStyles.HeaderResult
files.Summary: Result from CreateMainHeader containing references to update.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeDrawerStyles.Icons
files.Summary: Characters PlayForge's editors show as small icons in labels and buttons, each a string constant, as Check (✓), Cross (✗) and ArrowDown (↓).

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeDrawerStyles.SectionConfig
files.Summary: Configuration for collapsible section creation.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeDrawerStyles.SectionResult
files.Summary: Result from CreateCollapsibleSection containing references.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeDrawerStyles
files.Summary: Comprehensive UI building utilities for PlayForge editors. Provides all necessary methods to create custom editors programmatically.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeFlagsDrawer
files.Summary: A flags field of PlayForge's, which writes only what's picked. Unity's own flags field stores a value that holds every flag as Everything, -1, as it binds: an asset only looked at changed, as every effect's Purges' Applied By, Any by default; a template's child took the change as an override; and the inspector's SerializedObject moved while its bindings were still being made, which Unity asserted on (IsInSyncWithParentSerializedObject). This field shows the value without writing it, stores the flags picked of those its type has, so Everything is every flag it has now and not one it gains later, and follows an Undo.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeImportWindow.Field
files.Summary: One field the window can import, by its property path.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeImportWindow
files.Summary: The one Import window: choose a source, choose the fields that differ, each pre-checked, and import them as one Undo step. A list is replaced, unless its row asks to add to it. It serves a section's Import, a whole asset's, and a single property's, such as a worker group. A whole asset keeps its name, description, icons, asset tag, template and level link. Six windows did this before, each its own way: section import copied every field with no choice, and the Effect's Duration and Impact couldn't import.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeLint
files.Summary: What the project's assets give each other, which the content linter's checks read: the impact types its effects and impact workers deal, the gameplay events its thresholds and stop stages send, and the effects its items apply. It's gathered from every PlayForge asset, and the shared Value Pipelines and Effect Modifiers, as a check first asks, and forgotten as the validator checks the project afresh, or as an asset changes what it gives, which has every asset checked again against what's now true.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeLogSettingsBridge
files.Summary: Keeps the ForgeLog level chosen in Preferences → PlayForge and applies it to on every domain reload, since static fields reset on reload and EditorPrefs lasts.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeNewAssetWindow
files.Summary: A new asset's name and folder, then Create, as The Forge's Create menu asks. It makes the asset through the one factory a field's New uses too, : a copy of the type's New Asset default, named, with the tag its name gives, in the folder Project Settings names. The Create tab's dialog set type settings that did nothing, and logged each asset it made.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgePreset
files.Summary: A way to start a new asset: one of PlayForge's presets, which fills the new asset's fields, or one of the project's own template assets, which the new asset starts as a copy of.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgePresetMaking
files.Summary: What a preset reaches as it fills a new asset: its name, the project, and a way to make the assets it needs, each saved in its type's folder, or in the one the new asset was asked for where that isn't its type's.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgePresets
files.Summary: The presets The Forge's Create menu lists for each type: PlayForge's, then the project's templates.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeProblem
files.Summary: One problem the validator found in a PlayForge asset: the asset, how serious it is, and what's wrong.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeProblemSeverity
files.Summary: How serious a problem is: a Warning is likely a mistake, and an Error stops something working. A Note may be meant, as a trigger on an event that code sends: the Problems view lists it, and the counts and an inspector's header leave it out.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeProblemsWindow
files.Summary:
The Problems view: every problem the validator finds in the project's PlayForge assets, each with its severity and its asset, and a click selects the asset. It follows the validator, so it has no Refresh. It replaces Validate All, which showed 15 problems in a dialog nothing in could be selected, and the Audit, which wrote to the Console.

By Rule, its other view, groups the problems under the rule each breaks, and where a simple step fixes a problem, gives it a Quick Fix, and its rule a Fix All, each one Undo step.

It lists the linter's notes too, which may be meant, as a trigger on an event that code sends, under their own filter, and its counts leave them out.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeProjectEditor
files.Summary: A Forge Project's inspector: the shared header, then its settings; its catalog a line saying how many assets it names for saves and how it keeps them, where it drew each entry, a list of GUIDs as long as the project.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeQuickFix
files.Summary: A problem's quick fix: what it does, as its button says, and the step itself. The step writes through a SerializedObject, or records Undo, so the Undo step the Problems view opens around it takes it back; and the validator, which follows each edit, checks the asset again.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeRenameWindow
files.Summary: Rename, from an asset's menu in The Forge's list or its header, or F2 on The Forge's list: the asset's name, to type over, then Rename, which renames it as its inspector does (). Enter renames and Escape cancels.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeRenames
files.Summary: Renames an asset as its inspector does, from The Forge or an asset's header: a PlayForge asset's name, with the tag its name gives, as one Undo step; a Scaler asset's scaler and a Requirement template's requirements, whose names its lists show; and for an asset with no name of its own, as a Value Pipeline, its file alone. The file takes the name, with its type's prefix and suffix from Project Settings, leaving out its spaces as a new asset's file does, and follows the name back through Undo and Redo. A file that is its asset's only name keeps the spaces, and its rename Unity doesn't undo.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeSpreadsheetWindow
files.Summary: A sheet's changes before they're made: each number it changes, its asset, what it reads now and what it will, each chosen until it's unticked; what of the sheet can't be read; and Import, which makes the chosen changes as one Undo step.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeSpreadsheets
files.Summary:
Numbers by level and item stats, to and from CSV, so a game is balanced in a spreadsheet.

A sheet of numbers by level has a row for each number of an asset that reads a Table or By Level: the asset's tag and name, the field as the inspector labels it, its kind, and what it reads at each level, its values times its number, as Laguna Blade's -450/-600/-750. A sheet of item stats has a row for each item and a column for each attribute its granted effects add to: a number, or one for each level, as 10/15/20.

A sheet read back finds each row's asset by its asset tag, or by its name where it gives none; a name two assets share, an asset that isn't there and a field it hasn't got are problems, not guesses. Its changes, listed, apply as one Undo step, each number's values set so it reads what the row says.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeTagLibraryEditor
files.Summary: A Tag Library's inspector: the shared header, then its entries and its contexts.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeTagRegistry.ContextUsage
files.Summary: Tracks usage within a specific context.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeTagRegistry.FieldUsageInfo
files.Summary: Tracks a single usage of a tag - which asset and which field path.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeTagRegistry.TagContext
files.Summary: Represents a unique context where tags are used. Uses string-based context identifiers (from ForgeContext constants).

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeTagRegistry.TagUsageRecord
files.Summary: Tracks usage of a single tag across contexts.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeTagRegistry
files.Summary: Central registry for tracking tag usage across all PlayForge assets. Provides context-aware tag filtering and usage statistics.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeTemplateConfig
files.Summary: Defines which property paths are excluded from template propagation for each asset type. Excluded fields are identity fields (name, tags, textures), linking fields (link mode, linked source), and template system internals.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeTemplatePropagator
files.Summary:
Core engine for template propagation. Handles:

  • Propagating template field changes to child assets (non-overridden, non-excluded)
  • Merging list properties (additions and removals from template)
  • Detecting and recording field overrides by comparing child against template
  • Cascading propagation through template chains (A → B → C)
  • Finding all child assets of a given template via project scan

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeTemplatePush
files.Summary: Templates as prefabs work. A template's changes reach its children when it's pushed to them, as an explicit step: each child, and each of theirs, takes the template's fields but those it overrides, and one Undo takes the push back. An edit to a child's field makes the field the child's own, an override, which its inspector marks, and Revert to Template takes back. Saving a template opened a dialog in the middle of the save, loaded every asset of its type, and changed the children with no Undo.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeValidationRule
files.Summary: A check the validator runs on each PlayForge asset. Derive from it, with a public constructor that takes nothing, to add a check of your own: the validator finds every one. A problem a simple step fixes can carry the step as its .

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ForgeValidator
files.Summary: PlayForge's one validator. It runs every on each PlayForge asset in the project and keeps what they find, which the Problems view lists and an inspector's header counts. It follows the project, so nothing polls: an edit checks its asset again, an import checks what it brought, and a deleted asset has every asset checked again, since another may have read it. In batch mode, writes each problem to the Console. Validate All checked four things, flagged every effect with no workers, and showed 15 problems in a dialog.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.GameplayEffectDrawer
files.Summary: A reference to an effect: Unity's object field, with Open or New beside it, and under it a line that says how the effect takes its levels, with Link to make it take them from the asset that holds the field. Its right-click menu holds the field's template, a pick of the effects nothing links, and New Linked Effect. Setting the field asked in a dialog whether to link the effect, and the template, the link filter and a create button sat beside the field as tinted buttons.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.GameplayEffectDurationDrawer
files.Summary: An effect's duration: Policy, then what the policy uses: Duration and its ticks for a Durational effect, Tick Every for an Infinite one, then Tick On Application, execute ticks, the clock, Re-application and Then, and stacking for Stack Existing. It drew its parts in tinted boxes with colored headings, under sentences that explained them, and showed or hid them 50 ms after it drew. It follows the policy as it changes, an Undo among them.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.GameplayEffectEditor
files.Summary: The Effect inspector: Identity, Leveling, Tags, Duration, Impact, Requirements, Workers and Local Data, then Used By. A collapsed section shows one line, and the inspector takes its look from the style sheet. Requirements shows the target's table, then the source's, on a two-button switch.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.GameplayEffectImpactDrawer
files.Summary: An effect's impact: the attribute, the operation, the magnitude, then how the impact is delivered, which the duration gives it, and what a periodic one commits. Then its impact types and who it affects, its additional impacts, each with a delivery of its own, with Add Impact, and its contained effects. It no longer draws Reverse On Removal, which the impact model removed, and it takes its look from the style sheet: it drew tinted boxes with colored headings.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.IForgeComponentRule
files.Summary: A rule about one kind of component, whose problems an asset's inspector shows under its Components list.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.IProxyStagePolicyDrawer
files.Summary: A proxy stage's policy: its kind, named without "ProxyStagePolicy" or "Policy", always of some kind.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ImpactWorkerDrawer
files.Summary: An impact worker, as a worker group's Impact list holds one: its kind, picked from the impact workers or None, then its fields, folding to a line of their values.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.InlineFieldsDrawer
files.Summary: A field's own fields, drawn where it's held, as a component's own: a field of its whole drew a foldout inside the component.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ItemComponentDrawer
files.Summary: An item's component: its kind, never None and named without "ItemComponent", as "Uses" for a UsesItemComponent, then its fields, folding to a line of their values. A kind an item may hold only once isn't offered while its list holds one.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ItemDrawer
files.Summary: A reference to an item: Unity's object field, with Open or New beside it. It was a button that opened a dropdown list of its own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ItemEditor
files.Summary: The Item inspector: Identity, Leveling, Tags, the item's Effects and Abilities, Workers and Local Data, then Used By. A collapsed section shows one line, and the inspector takes its look from the style sheet.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.LevelProviderDrawer
files.Summary: A [LinkedSource] field, the asset whose levels this one takes: Unity's object field of level providers, whose picker lists them, and under it a line of the levels it gives. It was any asset's field that warned at a wrong pick, with a tinted box, a colored type badge, a × and a "..." that opened a browser window of its own, which Unity's picker does.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.LevelThresholdDrawer
files.Summary: A Threshold scaler's threshold: the level it holds from and the tier's name on one row, Unity's fields bound to them, so an Undo shows in them, and under them what the scaler reads from there, a number field of any kind. In a list it needs no label of its own. It drew a tinted row with "Lv" in blue and an arrow as text, and its fields wrote as they changed and followed nothing after.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.MagnitudeModifierGroupMemberDrawer
files.Summary: A Scaler Group's member, cached or not, as Unity's fields: how its result combines with the members' before it, then its scaler, whose own drawer shows its kind and its settings. It drew a stripe and a symbol in the operation's color, the scaler's kind beside them, and, for a cached member, a "CACHED" badge.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.NumberFields.Walk
files.Summary: How far walks into the numbers a value holds.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.NumberFields
files.Summary: What the number field's inspector and its Problems rule know of numbers: which properties are numbers, what a field's context provides and its unit, what a kind needs and where the kind menu files it, and what a number's kind reads, inside other scalers too.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.NumberLimits
files.Summary: The limits a number field's constant keeps in the inspector, from its , and , in what the field stores.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.NumberSiblingFieldDrawer
files.Summary: The field a relative number reads, picked from a menu of the other number fields of the object that holds the number, each by its name as the inspector writes it. The number's own field and any field that reads it back stay out, so a loop can't be picked. A name the object no longer has, as after a rename, shows as missing.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.PlayForgeGASProfilerModule
files.Summary: The PlayForge GAS module in Unity's Profiler: the GAS's counters, charted: its entities by hub, its effects, impacts, activations and refusals, and its tag compiles and recomputes.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.PlayForgePreferences
files.Summary: PlayForge's view toggles, which belong to each user rather than to the project, so they stay in EditorPrefs, as Unity's own preferences do, and the Preferences page edits them. The settings the project shares are .

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.PlayForgeProcessesProfilerModule
files.Summary: The PlayForge Processes module in Unity's Profiler: ProcessControl's and TaskSequence's counters, charted, and in its details the selected frame's costliest processes, which PlayForge puts into the capture as the frame's metadata while the Profiler records.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.PlayForgeSettings
files.Summary: PlayForge's authoring settings, a Forge Project's, so they travel with the project under version control: where each type's new assets go, the defaults a new asset copies and Import lists first, and the effects a new Cost or Cooldown copies. A new asset's file is its name alone. The Project Settings page edits them; the view toggles stay in Preferences (). The file and the EditorPrefs a project took them from once are gone with that taking.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.ProcessInstantiatorDrawer
files.Summary: A process's instantiator: its kind, or None, then its fields.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.PropertyFieldExtensions
files.Summary: Extensions to UI Toolkit's PropertyField: OnPopulated runs a callback once the field has built its children, at once where it has, or else on the field's scheduler, asking again until it has.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.PurgeFilterDrawer
files.Summary: A purge's filter: its kind, named without "Purge Filter", as Except Tagged, or one of your own, then the kind's own fields.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.QuickFillWizard.EFillPattern
files.Summary: The shape the values take from the first to the last.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.QuickFillWizard.ERounding
files.Summary: How the values are rounded once made.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.QuickFillWizard
files.Summary: Quick Fill, from a scaler field's menu: what it fills, the scaler's levels or its points; a pattern and its values; rounding; and a preview of the values as the scaler's table shows them, with their curve, and, for a scaler spread over levels, what each level reads between its points. Apply writes them, and the curve a spread scaler reads, as one Undo step. It drew a look of its own, a purple bold title, a green Apply, 10 px hints and tinted boxes, from styles set in C#, with its fields outside the label column, and wrote through a property it kept from when it opened.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.RelativeAttributeWorkerDrawer
files.Summary: A relative attribute worker, one made from AbstractRelativeAttributeWorker: its kind, picked from those workers or None, then its fields, folding to a line of their values.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.RequirementTemplateEditor
files.Summary: A Requirement Template's inspector: the shared header, then its fields.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.RespawnPlaceDrawer
files.Summary: A Respawn's place: its kind, Home, Where It Died or Point, or one of your own, named without "Respawn Place", then the kind's own fields, as Point's point.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.RuntimeDebugger
files.Summary: The Debugger: one window for the game as it plays, in place of the GAS Debugger, Process Control and the Tag Debugger. Its Entities view lists the hubs ProcessControl registers, of either kind, beside one hub's attributes, effects, abilities and tags, which it can change. Its Processes view lists every process, with what it's doing and how long its steps take, and its Tags view every tag the entities hold, as a tree, beside who holds the one selected. Its Timeline view shows what the entities' abilities and effects did over time, as a recorder heard it. The lists follow ProcessControl as processes join and leave, and the values change in place, at the rate the window menu sets, while the game plays. Outside Play mode it offers Play Mode. The GAS Debugger scanned the scene for MonoBehaviour hubs and rebuilt its details every 0.25 s; Process Control and the Tag Debugger were IMGUI windows of their own.

files.Title: FarEmerald.PlayForge.Editor.SaveScalerAssetWindow
